summary: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the Old Catholic Seminary of Amersfoort, the Sorbonne, and under Dasturs Darab and Kaus, later holding posts at the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres and Institut de France.

Abraham Richard Fuller was an Indologist and historian. A Major in the Royal Artillery and Lieutenant in the Bengal Army in 1849, he served as Director of the Department of Public Instruction in Punjab from 1860 to 1867.

Abraham Sachs was a historian, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Johns Hopkins University. He held positions at the Institute for Advanced Study in 1945 and Brown University from circa 1946 to 1983.

Abraham Yohannan was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson from circa 1894 to 1898 and held a post there from circa 1894 to 1925.
Abraham Zablocki works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested in 2008).
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under Anton Walter Florus Gueth from circa 1949 to 1952, Mahasi Sayadaw from circa 1952 to 1954, and U Nārada, and later taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, later working as a research associate at the University of Munich and Research Fellow at Hamburg.

Achyutananda Dash works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University (attested 1999).

Ada Maryla Falk was an Indologist and scholar of religion. She studied at the University of Florence under Paolo Emilio Pavolini and Sapienza University of Rome under Raffaele Pettazzoni, Carlo Formichi, and Giuseppe Tucci, later teaching at Calcutta and Sapienza.

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Martin Haug, as well as the University of Munich, before serving as Privatdozent at Göttingen and Professor at the University of Königsberg (1879–1921).

Adalbert J. Gail was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Helmut Hoffmann (~1964–1968) and held a post at the Free University of Berlin from circa 1978 to 2006.

Adalbert Kuhn was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and studied under Louis Poley. He held posts as teacher and director at Cöllnisches Gymnasium from 1837 to 1870.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at La Trobe University under Greg Bailey and became an Associate Professor in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland in 2009.

Adam Hardy is a South Asian art and architecture historian and Indologist who studied architecture at the University of Cambridge. He held professorships at De Montfort University (~1993–2004) and Cardiff University, and directed PRASADA.

Adam Heinz was a linguist who studied at the University of Lviv under Jerzy Kuryłowicz and completed his PhD at Jagiellonian University under Jan Safarewicz. He held posts at the Pedagogical University of Krakow and Jagiellonian University.
Adam Hohenberger was an Indologist and scholar of religion. He completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig between 1913 and 1918, where he studied under Ernst Windisch.

Adam Miller is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Chicago. He has held teaching posts at Western Illinois University, Heartland Community College, Towson University, and Mercyhurst University.

Adam Pearcey is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier. He is the founder, senior editor, and translator at Lotsawa House.

Adam Yuet Chau is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Stanford University. He served as a postdoctoral fellow at Harvard and became Professor of the Anthropology of China at the University of Cambridge in 2008.
Adele Schlombs is a scholar in sinology and history and archaeology. She held a post at the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln from circa 1991 to 2022.
